records.reasons: The design compares tutored with untutored students in a non-randomized internal pilot. That design supports a descriptive difference of 3 scale-score points. It does not support a causal claim, and it does not show the tutored and comparison groups were equivalent. Candidate B keeps the non-causal hedge in the headline summary. It also states the design limit (not randomized, possible selection) next to the numbers it qualifies. A board member who reads only the short version, or only the results line, gets the correct inference. Candidate A leaves the hedge only in the evaluator quote near the end, so the headline and the results line stand without a stated design limitation. A skimming reader could take the 11 versus 8 gap as an effect of the program. Neither candidate gives the uncertainty of the 3-point difference (standard error, effect size, comparison group size or baseline equivalence), and neither says whether 3 points is educationally meaningful. B is still clearly better for the stated purpose, because it keeps the claim within what the design supports. B also is closer to acting on the first read, because it tells the reader what the data can and cannot show before the budget vote. A caution about B: the phrase 'internal pilot comparison' is introduced for the first time in the revision. It may be a new characterization of the evidence rather than a preserved one. That is for the factual check, not a defect in the hedge itself.
